Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and Mike Thompson, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Johnson.

David Johnson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved exceptional reserve replacement ratios well above industry benchmarks, with organic growth highlighting the depth of our inventory. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on operating expenses per BOE, where we've hit historic lows through disciplined cost management. We are focused on maintaining top-tier environmental performance, with significant reductions in spills and incidents. Finally, we are taking steps to enhance refining segment efficiency, boosting throughput and margins amid volatile markets.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Lee: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $3.2 billion, up 18% year-over-year. Operating income was $850 million, and net income was $620 million. We generated $550 million in free cash flow and returned $250 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.2 billion in debt and $1.6 billion in cash.

Turning now to our operating expenses per BOE, or lease operating expenses—or LOE per BOE—a key metric that underscores our relentless focus on operational efficiency in this capital-intensive industry. Let me walk you through the trend analysis, the drivers behind our performance, and the cost management strategies that are positioning us for sustained free cash flow generation even in a sub-$70 WTI environment.

Starting with the headline: In Q3 2024, our company-wide LOE per BOE came in at $8.45, marking a robust 17% year-over-year decline from $10.18 in Q3 2023 and a sequential 4% improvement from $8.80 in Q2 2024. This represents the lowest quarterly LOE per BOE in our history as a public company, surpassing our previous low of $9.20 set in Q4 2023. For context, our trailing 12-month average now stands at $8.75 per BOE, down from $11.05 in the prior 12 months—a cumulative 21% reduction.

To put this in perspective, let's zoom out on the multi-year trend. Back in 2022, amid post-pandemic supply chain disruptions, steel price inflation exceeding 30%, and labor shortages driving wage premiums, our full-year LOE averaged $12.65 per BOE. That was a painful 18% jump from 2021 levels, largely due to elevated workover costs in our Bakken assets and weather-related downtime in the Gulf of Mexico. Fast-forward to 2023: aggressive cost controls helped us claw back to an annual average of $9.95 per BOE, a 21% improvement, even as natural gas prices languished below $3/MMBtu and curtailed offshore production amid Hurricane Idalia.

This year, 2024 year-to-date, we're tracking at $8.82 per BOE, putting us on pace for a full-year average below $8.70—our 2025 guidance midpoint. These aren't just top-line wins; they're flowing straight to the bottom line, contributing over $250 million in annualized LOE savings versus 2023 run rates, based on our Q3 production of 285,000 BOE per day.

Breaking it down regionally, our diversification is paying dividends. In the Permian Basin, which accounts for 62% of our production, LOE per BOE held steady at a market-leading $6.20—flat QoQ but down 22% YoY. This reflects the basin's natural economies of scale, with our Delaware sub-basin wells now averaging over 1,200 BOE per day in their first year. Key tailwinds here include optimized water management; we've cut produced water disposal costs by 25% through our partnership with WaterBridge Resources, recycling 65% onsite versus the basin average of 45%. Compare that to peers like Pioneer Natural Resources, who reported Permian LOE around $6.50 in their last quarter.

Shifting to the Eagle Ford, 22% of output, LOE rose modestly to $9.10 per BOE from $8.75 QoQ, driven by higher electricity costs amid Texas grid volatility and incremental ESP—electric submersible pump—deployments on our oilier Karnes County pads. Still, that's a 12% YoY drop, thanks to our shift to longer laterals averaging 12,000 feet, which spread fixed costs over 15% more BOE per well.

The Bakken (12% of production) saw the biggest sequential lift, with LOE at $11.50 per BOE, up from $10.90, primarily due to flaring curtailment compliance costs and saltwater disposal well permitting delays amid North Dakota's regulatory push. YoY, though, we're down 19%, outperforming Continental Resources' recent Bakken figures around $12.80.

Finally, our Gulf of Mexico shelf assets (4% of production) clocked in at $18.75 per BOE, elevated as expected due to fixed platform OPEX and subsea tie-back investments. But even here, we've trimmed 14% YoY through remote monitoring, avoiding a full shut-in during seasonal hurricanes.

Now, to the strategies fueling this trend—our 'Efficiency 2.0' program, launched mid-2023, is the backbone. We've deployed AI-driven predictive maintenance across 85% of our 4,200 producing wells, leveraging Schlumberger's Delfi platform. This has slashed unplanned downtime by 28%, from 3.2% to 2.3% of runtime, directly saving $0.45 per BOE in workover and lost production costs. In the Permian, IoT sensors on our 1,200 beam pump jacks have optimized stroke rates, reducing electricity usage by 15%—critical with ERCOT prices spiking 40% this summer.

On the supply chain front, we've locked in multi-year offtake agreements for tubular goods and chemicals at 2022 lows, hedging against the 12% steel inflation we saw earlier this year. Our vendor consolidation—down to top 50 suppliers from 120—yielded another 8% procurement savings, or $0.35 per BOE. Workforce optimization is key too: Digital twins and drone-based lease inspections have cut field crew hours by 22%, allowing us to maintain flat headcount despite 12% production growth.

Environmentally, these efficiencies align with our ESG goals—lower LOE means fewer truck turns for water hauling, cutting Scope 1 emissions by 18,000 MT CO2e YTD, and positioning us ahead of SEC climate disclosure rules.

Looking forward, we see continued tailwinds: WTI stabilizing around $72-75 should ease service cost pressures, while our Q4 base production guide of 290-300,000 BOE/d provides scale. We're targeting $8.10 per BOE in Q4 and a 2025 full-year average of $7.90-$8.30, assuming no major inflationary shocks. This supports our $1.2 billion capex plan and 15% dividend hike we announced today.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Thompson for an operational update, including our progress on proved reserves and other key areas.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought several new pads online in the Permian and Eagle Ford, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

As we wrap up on operations, let me address our environmental performance, specifically spills, incidents, and remediation efforts—a cornerstone of our ESG commitments at Apex Energy Corp. We remain steadfast in our goal of zero environmental incidents, aligning with our net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions target by 2050, and we're making measurable progress amid a challenging macroeconomic environment with Brent crude hovering around $75 per barrel and heightened regulatory scrutiny from the EPA and BSEE.

Let me start with the numbers. In Q3, we recorded three reportable spills, a 50% reduction from the five incidents in Q3 last year and well below the industry average of 4.2 spills per quarter for majors, per API data. Total spill volume was 47 barrels—predominantly light crude and produced water—representing a 65% year-over-year decline from 135 barrels. On a normalized basis, our spill rate stands at 0.12 barrels per million barrels produced, outperforming peers like Chevron's 0.18 and ExxonMobil's 0.15, as reported in their latest sustainability filings. This metric has improved 28% sequentially from Q2's 0.17 rate, driven by proactive integrity management.

Diving deeper into incidents, our total environmental incident rate—encompassing spills, leaks, and unauthorized discharges—dropped to 0.04 incidents per 200,000 man-hours worked, a new company low and 20% below the IOGP benchmark of 0.05 for upstream operations. No Tier 1 process safety events occurred, maintaining our perfect streak for eight straight quarters. Flaring volumes were down 15% quarter-over-quarter to 1.2% of gross production, thanks to enhanced vapor recovery units at our Permian assets, where we routed an additional 450 MMcf of associated gas back into processing.

Regionally, performance was strong across the board. In the Permian Basin, our largest footprint with 650,000 boe/d net production, we had one minor spill of 22 barrels of produced water from a third-party saltwater disposal wellhead failure—fully contained within secondary containment berms. Remediation wrapped in 48 hours at a cost of $150,000, with zero groundwater impact confirmed by third-party hydrogeological surveys. This incident underscores the value of our $25 million investment in automated wellhead monitoring, using IoT sensors and SCADA integration, which flagged pressure anomalies 12 hours pre-failure.

Offshore in the Gulf of Mexico, where we operate six platforms including our flagship Dorado FPSO, we reported zero spills—our best quarter since acquiring the assets from Shell in 2022. Pipeline integrity runs via ILI (In-Line Inspection) tools detected and preempted two potential corrosion sites on our 48-inch Dorado export line, averting what could have been a 100+ barrel event. Our subsea robotics program, deploying ROVs with 4K imaging and acoustic leak detection, achieved 99.8% leak-free uptime, aligning with BOEM's stringent SEMS II requirements.

In the North Sea, our Buzzard field JV with Suncor and TotalEnergies saw one 25-barrel crude spill from a loading hose coupling on the FPSO during offloading ops—immediately boomed and skimmed with dispersant-approved response vessels. This was 40% below our five-year average, thanks to our adoption of the Oil Spill Modelling toolkit from SINTEF, which simulated plume dispersion in real-time for optimal deployment of our 2,500-meter boom capacity.

On remediation, we're not just reactive—we're restorative. All Q3 spills achieved 100% recovery or natural attenuation, with bioremediation applied at the Permian site using ExxonMobil's Proven microbes, degrading 95% of hydrocarbons within 72 hours per EPA Method 5035 analytics. Total remediation spend was $1.2 million, flat YoY despite 12% production growth, equating to just 0.02% of our $6.2 billion capex budget. We've reclaimed 150 acres of disturbed land this year under our Progressive Reclamation program, planting native species in the Bakken shale play, boosting biodiversity scores by 18% in independent audits from ERM.

Strategically, these results stem from our $150 million 2024 HSE tech roadmap, including: AI-driven predictive analytics—partnering with Schlumberger's Delfi platform, we've reduced leak probabilities by 35% across 5,000 miles of pipeline through ML models trained on 10 years of ILI and cathodic protection data. Drone and satellite surveillance: Weekly hyperspectral drone flights over Permian pads detected 22 micro-leaks totaling 5 barrels before they escalated, with integration into our AspenTech OSIsoft PI system for real-time dashboards. Materials innovation: Rolling out HDPE-lined composite pipes from Shawcor, cutting corrosion rates by 40% in sour gas environments, and our first deployment of solid-state hydrogen sensors for early methane detection.

Looking ahead, we're positioning Apex for the energy transition. Regulatory tailwinds like the IRA's methane fees have us ahead of compliance, with emissions intensity at 8.2 kg CO2e/boe—15% below the 2023 API peer median. We've avoided $10 million in potential fines this year through preemptive abatements, directly accretive to FCF. Our ESG credit facility with JPMorgan ties $500 million in low-cost debt to spill rate targets, and we're on track for S&P Global's BBB sustainability rating upgrade.

In summary, our environmental performance isn't just compliance—it's a competitive moat, enabling premium access to capital and JV partnerships amid OPEC+ cuts and LNG demand surges. We're proud of these outcomes and committed to continuous improvement.

Now, shifting to our refining segment performance, where we delivered another strong quarter amid a volatile macro environment. Our refining portfolio consists of six high-complexity refineries with a total nameplate capacity of 1.8 million barrels per day, spanning the U.S. Gulf Coast, Midwest PADD 2, and our joint venture assets in Europe. Our fleet boasts an average Nelson Complexity Index of 11.2, positioning us well for value-added product yields like ULSD, jet fuel, and premium gasoline.

Starting with throughput, we averaged 1.52 million barrels per day in Q3, representing 95% utilization of our atmospheric distillation units—up 3% sequentially from Q2's 1.48 MMbpd and flat year-over-year. This resilience came despite planned turnarounds at our Port Arthur and Memphis facilities, where we successfully completed major maintenance on hydrocrackers and alkylation units ahead of schedule, minimizing unplanned downtime to just 1.2%. Gulf Coast throughput hit a record 1.05 MMbpd, fueled by robust light sweet crude imports from the Permian and Eagle Ford, while our Midwest plants operated at 98% utilization, capitalizing on Canadian heavy sour crudes discounted against WTI. Regionally, PADD 3 demand remained strong with summer driving season underway, though we saw softer jet throughput in Europe due to lingering post-COVID travel normalization—down 2% QoQ but still 15% above 2022 levels.

On margins, we realized a segment EBITDA of $850 million, or $18.50 per barrel sold, a 25% increase from Q2's $14.80/bbl and well ahead of consensus expectations. This was driven by healthy crack spreads, with the 3-2-1 Gulf Coast average settling at $24.50/bbl—up from $19.20 in Q2—supported by gasoline cracks averaging $28/bbl on RBOB futures strength and ULSD at $32/bbl amid trucking demand. Our realized product slate pricing rose 8% QoQ to $105/bbl, outpacing feedstock costs at $78/bbl, yielding a 2:1 products-to-feed ratio. We benefited from our hedging program, locking in 60% of Q4 cracks at $22/bbl floors, which shielded us from the mid-quarter WTI-Brent backwardation. Notably, our renewable diesel margins held firm at $1.20/gallon after RIN values stabilized around $1.50/D4 RIN, with our Martinez co-processing unit hitting 15,000 bpd of HRD production—fully contracted through 2025 with West Coast offtakers.

Operational efficiency was a standout, with total cash operating costs per barrel declining 7% YoY to $6.20/bbl, thanks to a suite of technical initiatives rolled out post our 2023 digital transformation roadmap. We achieved a 2% improvement in clean product yields to 88% of crude input, driven by advanced process control upgrades on our fluid catalytic crackers at Corpus Christi, boosting gasoline octane by 1.5 RON without incremental capex. Predictive analytics via our AI-powered digital twin platform reduced energy intensity by 4%—saving 15,000 MT of CO2e—and preempted 85% of potential outages, lifting mechanical availability to 99.1%. In Europe, our Rotterdam JV optimized VGO hydrotreating for IMO 2020-compliant LSFO, capturing a $5/bbl premium on exports to Asia. These efforts not only enhanced reliability but also positioned us ahead of peers like Valero and Phillips 66, where we've outpaced their utilization by 400 bps on a trailing 12-month basis.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on high-grades resilience and low-carbon transitions. We've greenlit $450 million in 2025 capex for renewable fuels expansion, including a 20,000 bpd HRD train at our East Coast facility, targeting 10% of throughput from biofuels by 2027 to capture IRA incentives and LCFS credits. Upstream-downstream synergies remain key: our proprietary Permian crudes shaved $2/bbl off Gulf Coast feedstocks, while trading desks arbitraged 50,000 bpd of sweet-sour differentials. Looking forward, we see Q4 throughput at 1.55 MMbpd with 92% utilization, assuming no hurricanes disrupt the Gulf, and margins sustaining in the mid-teens on seasonal distillate strength. Risks include potential CREDA outages or RIN volatility, but our $1.2 billion liquidity buffer and flexible turnaround cadence give us optionality.

Finally, let's dive into our proved reserves additions, reserve replacement ratio—or RRR—and organic growth. In our industry, maintaining a robust reserve base is the lifeblood of long-term value creation, ensuring we can deliver multi-decade inventory at competitive half-cycle returns. At the end of Q3 2024, our total proved reserves stood at 2.6 billion barrels of oil equivalent—or BOE—up 8% from year-end 2023. We added 480 million BOE of proved reserves through all sources, net of production. This translates to a total reserve replacement ratio of 418%—well above our long-term target of 150% and in line with top-tier peers like EOG Resources and Pioneer Natural Resources, who posted RRRs north of 300%.

Even more impressively, our organic reserve replacement ratio—excluding acquisitions and divestitures—clocked in at 335%. That's organic additions of 385 million BOE, driven purely by our exploration success, development drilling, and revisions from better reservoir performance. This marks our fifth straight year of organic RRR exceeding 200%, with a three-year average of 285%. This isn't luck; it's the result of disciplined capital allocation and technological edge in high-margin plays.

Breaking it down by source, extensions and discoveries accounted for 62% of organic additions, or 240 million BOE, primarily from successful delineation in our core acreage. Positive revisions from proved developed producing—or PDP—properties added another 105 million BOE, fueled by outperformance in our shale assets where we've optimized frac designs and extended lateral lengths to over 15,000 feet. Improved recovery techniques contributed 40 million BOE, including early pilots of CO2 foam EOR in the Permian. We had negligible negative revisions, thanks to our rigorous reservoir engineering and data analytics—our proprietary AI-driven reservoir simulation models, which integrate real-time production data with 4D seismic, have reduced uncertainty by 25% in our type curves.

Regionally, the Permian Basin remains our powerhouse, delivering 55% of organic additions, or 210 million BOE. In the Delaware Basin, our Northern Rustler Breaks position expanded by 120 million BOE through 12 successful horizontal Wolfcamp A and C wells, where we've achieved average 30-day IPs of 1,800 BOE/d per well at sub-$35 WTI breakevens. This reflects our pad-drilling efficiency—now averaging 8 wells per pad—and cube development strategy, which minimizes surface footprint and NRI dilution. Year-over-year, Permian organic RRR hit 450%, positioning us with a 12-year drilling inventory at $50 WTI.

In the Eagle Ford, we added 85 million BOE organically, with standout results from our Karnes Trough acreage. Here, we've refined our super-lateral program in the Lower Eagle Ford shale, pushing laterals to 18,000 feet and incorporating engineered completions with diverter tech from Halliburton. This drove a 15% uplift in estimated ultimate recovery—or EURs—to 1.2 MBOE per 1,000-foot lateral, sustaining a 280% organic RRR despite flat production.

Our offshore Gulf of Mexico assets punched above their weight, contributing 65 million BOE in organic additions from the Lobster field tie-back and a new sidetrack discovery in Mississippi Canyon Block 398. Leveraging high-resolution 3D OBN seismic—ocean-bottom node—we converted 40 million BOE of probable reserves to proved, with first oil expected in Q4 2024 at under $45 Brent breakeven. This segment's organic RRR exceeded 500%, highlighting our deepwater expertise amid peers like Chevron scaling back GOM due to higher capex intensity.

Internationally, our Brazil pre-salt venture with Petrobras added 25 million BOE via positive revisions in the Buzios field phase 3 development. While still ramping, this positions us for 20% CAGR in international reserves through 2027.

Strategically, these results affirm our 'organic first' philosophy. We've grown proved undeveloped—or PUD—reserves by 15% to 1.1 billion BOE, with 85% liquids-rich and 70% in tiers 1 and 2 inventory—defined as locations with >20% IRR at $50 WTI. This de-risks our long-term plan, supporting 5-7% annual production growth through the decade without chasing M&A premiums. Post-2020 service cost deflation and our in-house frac fleet have compressed D&C costs by 22% since 2019, enabling faster conversions from PUD to PDP.

Looking ahead, we're on track for 300-350 million BOE in organic additions in 2024, targeting a sustained 250%+ organic RRR. Initiatives like our Permian waterflood pilots and machine learning for sweet-spot mapping will further enhance recoveries. ESG-wise, our low-methane capture rates—under 0.2%—and electrified fracs align reserves growth with net-zero ambitions.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Walsh with Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.

Brian Walsh: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the operating expenses per BOE trends and how sustainable they are?

David Johnson: Good question, Brian. As Sarah detailed, our LOE hit a record low of $8.45 per BOE this quarter, driven by Efficiency 2.0 and regional optimizations like Permian water recycling. We see this trending to $7.90-$8.30 in 2025, supporting robust FCF even at lower prices.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for refining margins and throughput going into Q4?

Sarah Lee: Thanks, Lisa. We're guiding Q4 throughput to 1.55 MMbpd at 92% utilization, with mid-teens margins on strong distillate cracks. Hedging and synergies from upstream keep us resilient.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera: Could you please provide more color on environmental incidents and remediation?

Mike Thompson: Absolutely, Tom. We had just three small spills totaling 47 barrels, down sharply YoY, with 100% remediation via tech like AI leak detection. This keeps us ahead on ESG and avoids fines.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Johnson for closing remarks.

David Johnson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
